key_insight: Representing Chain-of-Thought as executable code ("Code-as-CoT") provides precise, structured intermediate plans for text-to-image generation, enabling accurate spatial layouts, dense text, and rare concept rendering via previews and stepwise refinement.
problem_solved: Natural-language CoT is too imprecise for complex spatial composition, structured visual elements, and rare concepts; CoCo addresses this by producing formal, executable plans that bridge language and image synthesis.
method: Translate natural-language prompts into short, executable code snippets (scene descriptions, SVG/layout primitives, or rendering instructions) that serve as explicit, inspectable CoT.
Execute or simulate the code to produce a visual preview and use the structured output to condition a T2I model, enabling iterative refinement and improved grounding of rare concepts.
Train/align the UMM to interpret code outputs and integrate code-driven planning into generation, improving fidelity for dense text, layout-sensitive scenes, and uncommon objects.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical way to get interpretable previews and fine-grained control over T2I outputs, improving reliability for design, data augmentation, and generation of rare concepts; reduces trial-and-error prompt engineering.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Prompt → Code-as-CoT → Executable preview → T2I model → Final image
Side-by-side comparisons: NL-CoT outputs vs Code-as-CoT outputs highlighting layout/text fidelity and rare-concept accuracy
Code snippet + rendered preview: small code block (e.g., SVG-like) next to its visual preview to show executability
Interactive UI mock: preview + editable code pane demonstrating user-in-the-loop refinement
paper_title: CoCo: Code as CoT for Text-to-Image Preview and Rare Concept Generation
paper_authors: Haodong Li, Chunmei Qing, Huanyu Zhang, Dongzhi Jiang, Yihang Zou
